newsitem.title: USA: Republican leader backs Clinton on liquor ad ban.
newsitem.headline: Republican leader backs Clinton on liquor ad ban.

text.p: Senate Republican leader Trent Lott on Sunday strongly backed President Bill Clinton's opposition to liquor advertisements on television and radio.
"Absolutely, I join him in that effort," the Mississippi senator said on NBC Television's "Meet the Press" programme when asked about Clinton's criticism of the liquor advertising.
Clinton on Saturday called the U.S. liquor industry "irresponsible" for deciding to drop a decades-old ban on television and radio advertisements.
"You're wrong to change your policy now," the president said in his weekly radio address. "This is no time to turn back. Get back on the ban. That's the best way to protect all our families."
Lott said this "would have a bad impact on our children, on society as a whole. That is totally wrong."
The liquor industry's trade association, the Distilled Spirits Council of the United States, said last week it would end the voluntary ban on advertising of hard liquor.
The ban had been in effect since 1936 for radio and 1948 for television. Seagram Co Ltd had begun defying the ban in June by running commercials for its Royal Crown whiskey in selected local markets.
Four television networks, CBS, NBC, ABC and Fox, have said they will not run liquor ads. Together they own about 50 stations in major markets.
There are just under 1,200 commercial stations scattered across the nation not owned by the major networks that could be targeted by the liquor industry.
